NC_CONF.question: A plastic scintillator calorimeter wall is built from cells, each read one-to-one by its own photomultiplier tube with a 76 mm diameter, mounted inside a thin magnetic shield and directly coupled to the back face of the cell, with no light guide. Can such a wall be segmented finely enough that any two particles entering it at points 6 cm apart are always recorded in different cells? End your answer with one line: VERDICT: YES or VERDICT: NO.
